title: Water and ice on Home Street North at Loewen Boulevard
ask: Fix the open drainage swale that sends water (and ice) across Home Street North near Loewen Boulevard.
tactics: Short email to council, after earlier discussions with staff; timed to an unusual freeze-thaw December when the open swale across the street was icing.
outcome_detail: Council reached consensus (no motion) to have administration monitor the spot and report back on options and costs; no report or repair appears in the 2016 transcripts. Home Street residents returned with a petition delegation on 2017-02-07.
vote: not recorded (consensus to request a staff report)
notes: The email's exact wording is not in the transcript. Speaker E ('Councillor Pannett') is one of the two Penners; not identified. Follow-up petition (2017-02-07) belongs to the 2017 period.

title: Summer in the City festival grant request
ask: A city grant for the Summer in the City festival (amount not stated in the transcript).
tactics: Grant request letter on the agenda in December, ahead of budget deliberations.
outcome_detail: The mayor said the request would be considered in budget discussions; no public decision on the amount was found in the 2016 transcripts. Council set up a city-appointed governing board for the festival in November 2016.
notes: Amount and outcome not verifiable without minutes or the 2016 financial plan detail.

title: Other grant and advocacy letters filed without action (2016)
requester: Manitoba Crime Stoppers; Bethesda Foundation; permanent animal shelter supporters; Canadian Union of Postal Workers; L.P. (resident, PTH 52 West); Invasive Species Council of Manitoba; Mr. T. (resident)
ask: Various: Crime Stoppers grant request (2016-02-02); Bethesda Foundation letter (2016-01-19, content not read out); a permanent animal shelter support request (2016-09-06); CUPW form letter asking councils to back restoring home mail delivery (2016-07-05); L.P.'s letter on Provincial Trunk Highway 52 West (2016-10-18); Invasive Species Council letter (2016-12-06); Mr. T.'s letter (2015-12-15).
tactics: Letters placed on the agenda under correspondence, without a delegation.
outcome_detail: Each was taken as information with no action, usually without discussion.
notes: The content of the Bethesda Foundation, Invasive Species Council, L.P. and Mr. T. letters is not described in the transcripts, so whether each was an ask is unverified. Excluded as not requests: Hanover School Division letter (2016-03-15), Steinbach MCC letter on the performing arts centre (2016-03-01), Valiant Canada (2016-01-19), Shaw Canada 150 letter (forwarded to ROCK Steinbach, 2016-11-15), provincial grant letters.

title: Year-long mobile sign permits
ask: Loosen the mobile sign rules so businesses can keep signs up longer (annual permits instead of 30 days on, 30 off, 90 days a year).
tactics: Businesses complained after enforcement of the new 2015 zoning bylaw's 30-day mobile sign limit; council took it up at committee and initiated an amendment.
outcome_detail: Bylaw 2066 extending mobile sign permits to 365 days got first reading on 2015-12-15 (two councillors opposed) and second and third readings on 2016-01-19; no one objected at the public hearing.
mover: first reading: councillor labelled D, probably Michael Zwaagstra; second reading: Michael Zwaagstra; third reading: Earl Funk
seconder: first: John Fehr; second: Earl Funk; third: Michael Zwaagstra
vote: first reading carried with Jac Siemens and one Councillor Penner speaking against; second and third carried (opposition called, not counted)
notes: The original business complaints (fall 2015) predate this period and are not in these transcripts.

title: Sidewalk with the Old Tom Road paving
requester: Mr. and Mrs. T. (Lyons Gate residents)
ask: Add a sidewalk along Old Tom Road as part of the planned paving project.
tactics: Letter added to the agenda as late correspondence, timed to the Old Tom Road paving project; included the writers' own estimate of the sidewalk cost.
outcome_detail: Council agreed (no motion) not to tie a sidewalk to the paving, which staff said could nearly double the $1 million project, and to consider it later in the overall sidewalk plan. The paving tender went ahead in May 2016 without a sidewalk.
notes: The letter-writers are identified only as 'Mr. and Mrs. Taves on Lyons Gate' in the transcript; shown by initials. No minutes for 2016.

title: Chamber of Commerce: rewrite the mobile sign bylaw with business
ask: Strike an ad hoc committee of 3 councillors and 3 Chamber representatives to write an entirely new mobile sign bylaw; later, keep 1-foot setbacks so existing signs stay usable.
tactics: Delegation arranged after a talk between the mayor and the Chamber's director; prepared written statement; specific structure (3 councillors, 3 Chamber reps, staff); later returned to the public hearing with drawings of three affected businesses (Shoppers Drug Mart, Quality Details, Good and Natural).
outcome_detail: No ad hoc committee was publicly struck; staff drafted amendments using Chamber and business submissions. After the Chamber's public-hearing objection, council cut the setback to 1 foot for all mobile signs (2016-10-18) and passed the amendments on 2016-11-01, crediting the Chamber's input.
mover: setback amendment: Michael Zwaagstra; third reading: John Fehr
seconder: setback amendment: Earl Funk; third reading: Earl Funk
vote: setback amendment carried (opposition called, not counted); second and third readings carried
notes: Committee of council as a whole sessions are not recorded, so whether an informal joint group met is unknown. The 2016-10-18 setback request was made at a public hearing on the city's own bylaw amendment, not a planning application.

title: Ask Hanover School Division to freeze school taxes
ask: Council formally asks Hanover School Division to consider freezing taxes in 2016.
tactics: Councillor's motion citing residents' complaints about rising tax bills and the city's own four-year freeze; school taxes about 55% of the bill.
outcome_detail: Motion carried; the mayor said he would also follow up in person with the division. At least Councillor Siemens said he would vote against, preferring a meeting before a formal letter.
vote: carried; opposition called but not counted (Siemens said he would vote against)
notes: The turn at 0:21:13 announcing a vote against is labelled F (Funk's label) but the mayor answers 'Councillor Seaman's suggestion that we should meet with them', so it was Siemens; not quoted for that reason. Whether HSD acted is outside the transcripts.

title: Drainage at Loewen Boulevard and Old Tom Road property
ask: City action on water accumulating on his property near the provincial drain.
tactics: Repeat letter (not the first about this property) describing long-standing water on the back of his lot, which sits on an old creek bed beside a provincial drain.
outcome_detail: No action and no decision: staff said improvements to such drains come only with development and the drain is provincial; the deputy mayor said upstream talks with the conservation district and golf course were at an early stage.
notes: 'Pincott' appears to be a transcription of Earl Funk's name (on 2016-07-19 the seconder 'Councilor Funk' is then asked 'Councillor Pincott, anything further?'), but this is inferred.

title: Canadian Blood Services: council to champion the local clinic
ask: Councillors promote the clinic through their networks and pledge to help grow it; implied request for a supporting resolution like Gimli's Partners for Life resolution.
tactics: Registered delegation with local numbers (largest community clinic in Manitoba, 1,572 units, switch to biweekly clinics needing about 750 donors); peer example of the RM of Gimli's resolution and mayors of Morris, Gimli and Portage greeting donors.
outcome_detail: No questions and no resolution; the mayor said the information would be distributed to staff.
notes: Rated 'partly' because a staff distribution (what Gimli also did) was offered but no resolution or pledge.

title: Headway at-risk youth program: city funding
requester: Headway Program / B.B., with RCMP Steinbach detachment (H.L.)
ask: A city contribution toward a remaining $20,000 shortfall, ideally a yearly amount.
tactics: Delegation with program model, outcomes and cost-of-crime research; budget of about $70,000 with $18,000 in-kind from Hanover School Division and RCMP; RCMP staff sergeant backed it at the same meeting and asked for a yearly amount; followed by a letter.
outcome_detail: The mayor promised a response citing the city's grant policy; the follow-up funding letter was received as information on 2016-06-07. A further Headway funding letter was again taken as information on 2017-11-21.
notes: The RCMP officer is shown by initials as a delegate. Credit to 'Susan and Kerry' is the officer's statement, not verified.

title: Steinbach North commercial park: swale drainage instead of storm sewer
requester: Steinbach Land Holding Partners / Northview Developments (D.C., B.S.)
ask: Exempt the development from city construction specs to allow swale (ditch) drainage with no curb and gutter.
tactics: Two delegations a month apart; framed as an 'upgrade' from an approved bare-land condo to a registered subdivision (gravity sewer, 32-foot concrete streets); cited the city's Hespeler industrial park precedent, signed buyers (Petro-Canada), a neighbour's support letter, $800,000 a year in future taxes and the construction season.
outcome_detail: On 2016-04-05 a motion to approve was withdrawn for lack of detail. On 2016-05-03 council approved a one-time exception through a development agreement (gravity sewer, piped water, 32-foot concrete street, swale drainage, no curb and gutter), against the city manager's advice.
vote: carried; Zwaagstra said he would vote against (count not recorded)
notes: Diarization is poor in both meetings (delegate and councillor turns merged under one label), so only clearly attributable turns are quoted.

title: Speeding on Old Tom Road
requester: Clear Spring Green resident (name not read)
ask: Traffic control to deal with speeding on Old Tom Road.
tactics: Letter timed to the Old Tom Road paving project.
outcome_detail: Staff said a traffic count was being analysed and any recommendations would come to council after paving, in late summer or fall, in a package with other pending traffic-control requests; no such decision was found in the 2016 transcripts. Council asked that the resident be told the process.
notes: The councillor (label D) who asked that the resident be replied to is not identified.

title: Eastman Tourism: city membership
ask: Join Eastman Tourism ($1,500 a year, prorated) and name a city contact for tourism.
tactics: Delegation with written package; tourism spending and tax figures; Steinbach the only major urban centre not a member; tied to the Manitoba Summer Games in August 2016; prorated fee offered.
outcome_detail: Council asked two questions and thanked the delegation; no decision on membership appears in the 2016 or 2017 transcripts.
notes: A councillor (label H) asked whether the city had ever been a member; not identified.

title: Fly-In Golf Club: water management, compensation and a yearly grant
ask: Four asks: an active partnership on water flowing through the course; compensation of about $675,000 for past costs; future funding for flood damage; a $50,000 yearly recreation grant.
tactics: Delegation timed after council's summer study session; history of 2002 and 2007 presentations; damage and lost-revenue figures (about $675,000 in costs, about $48,000 a year in closures); peer comparison with other towns' golf clubs; written request circulated.
outcome_detail: The mayor said the requests would go through the budget process ending in November; no public decision appears in 2016. In December 2017 Councillor Zwaagstra said a $500,000 grant request made in a closed meeting about a year earlier had been denied and was replaced by a $500,000 land purchase and lease-back (approved 2017-12-05).
notes: The 2017 closed-meeting account is Councillor Zwaagstra's (2017-12-05) and belongs to the 2017 period; not verified against minutes here.

title: Dog park
requester: Councillor Penner (probably Susan Penner), for residents
ask: Staff report on possible dog park locations and a ballpark cost.
tactics: Councillor's motion after years of residents raising it while door-knocking; linked to a pending increase in dog licence fees that could pay for it.
outcome_detail: Motion for a staff report carried; no report or dog park appears in the later 2016 or 2017 transcripts.
notes: Medium-confidence speaker used for the named quote, as stated.

title: Waive a drainage-plan condition on a variance
ask: Drop the requirement to commission a lot drainage plan attached to his variance approval.
tactics: Letter (pages 83-85 of the agenda) after an earlier appearance at council; argued the $2,000-$3,000 plan was unfair for a single older lot and neighbours got along.
outcome_detail: Council agreed (no motion) that the city's drainage policy stands and asked administration to tell him so.
notes: The earlier variance hearing (a planning matter) is not counted as a request.

title: Sidewalk on Albert Street
ask: Build a sidewalk on Albert Street.
tactics: Letter citing busier traffic near the new primary health care centre; offered to canvass neighbours for support.
outcome_detail: Council voted for a staff report on cost and background for possible 2017 budgeting; no report appears in the transcripts, and in July 2017 the city manager said there were no immediate plans for a sidewalk there.
notes: The 2017-07-18 comment by the city manager is in the 2017 transcripts.

title: Haven Group: development fee rebate for 55+ housing
ask: Rebate of city development fees for the 55+ housing project.
tactics: Letter tied to a planned 55+ seniors housing expansion beside Woodhaven Manor; compared to a past city seniors housing grant program.
outcome_detail: Council asked administration to send the old program's criteria (supportive or assisted living confirmed by Southern Health) and ask whether the project qualified; no decision on the rebate appears later in 2016. The project's rezoning was approved on 2016-10-18 (a planning matter).
notes: Likely a de facto refusal, but no public decision was found.

title: Name a street after pioneer Cornelius Taves
ask: Recognize Cornelius Taves with a street name.
tactics: Letter with local history about one of the original settlers' land scouts.
outcome_detail: Because developers choose street names, council agreed administration would forward the request to local developers; no street was named by council.
notes: Whether any developer used the name was not checked.

title: Allow digital (illuminated) mobile signs
ask: Change the bylaw ban on illuminated or electrified mobile signs so a digital mobile display trailer can be used.
tactics: Spoke at the public hearing on the sign bylaw amendment; pointed to digital mobile signs in Winkler, on PTH 52 and in Winnipeg, and to the Manitoba Summer Games' use of one.
outcome_detail: Council first sent the bylaw back for review of illuminated signs (carried 2016-10-18), but staff advised that adding digital mobile signs would need a new public hearing; council passed the bylaw without them on 2016-11-01 and deferred the idea to a future zoning bylaw review (18 months to 2+ years away).
vote: referral carried 2016-10-18; bylaw passed without the change 2016-11-01
notes: Raised during a public hearing on a city-initiated bylaw amendment; included because it was a new request, not an objection to a planning application.

title: Mobile sign on the city right-of-way
ask: Allow its mobile sign to stand in the public right-of-way.
tactics: Letter added to the agenda two weeks after the sign bylaw was finalized.
outcome_detail: Taken as information by consensus; the rule against signs in the right-of-way stands and administration was to tell the owner.

title: Chamber of Commerce annual grant (business tax pass-through)
ask: Continue forwarding the Chamber's share of business tax revenue (less a 5% collection fee).
tactics: Annual letter of request with financial statements, under a standing arrangement.
outcome_detail: Taken as information because the arrangement is ongoing and is approved through the annual financial plan; in March 2017 council was told the city collects the levy and turns it over to the Chamber.
notes: Rated 'won' on the strength of the ongoing arrangement; the 2017 budget line was not checked.

title: Grant requests from the city's core organizations
requester: Mennonite Heritage Village; Steinbach Chamber of Commerce
ask: Annual operating grants.
tactics: Annual grant letters from organizations the city funds as 'core' partners.
outcome_detail: Taken as information and left to the budget ('covered off in our core 4 organizations'; Chamber request 'dealt with in the budget'). No 2017 decision is on record because budgets were set outside the regular meetings.
vote: received as information; deferred to budget
notes: Mennonite Heritage Village also sent a grant request on Nov 21 (taken as information 'for now'). Likely funded through the 2017/2018 budgets; not verified.

title: Home Street North drainage swale
ask: Rebuild the Home Street North swale so water flows under the road (culvert) instead of over it.
tactics: Delegation with a petition from neighbours, after earlier letters to administration in 2016; presenter cited his professional background in land and water management; safety and city-liability argument; framed the over-the-road swale as 'small-town thinking' in a city building a performing arts centre.
outcome_detail: Council asked administration for options and costs (Feb 7). The Dec 5 report found a piped crossing or bridge would cost about $500,000 plus property purchases (the mayor paraphrased it as over $1 million); only extra monitoring and maintenance continued, no action was taken, and the mayor asked that petitioners be told the cost.
mover: Councillor Cari Penner (medium confidence; motion for an options-and-cost report)
vote: not recorded (carried, Feb 7 report request); no motion on Dec 5 report
notes: The Feb 7 chair was addressed as 'Mr. Deputy Mayor'; John Fehr was deputy mayor until Nov 2017 (per the Nov 7 organization meeting). Which Penner moved the Feb 7 motion is inferred (medium). No later minutes for 2017 were available to confirm whether a letter went to petitioners. Street name corrected from the transcript's "Holmes Street" to Home Street North (per later minutes).

title: Open the Aquatic Centre on statutory holidays
requester: Councillor Penner, for families (Family Day users)
ask: Open the Aquatic Centre on statutory holidays such as Louis Riel Day (Family Day).
tactics: Raised in question period the day after Family Day; a second councillor cited families on Facebook looking for things to do; staff report used informal public surveys showing high interest; motion offset the extra cost by closing on Remembrance Day (net one extra day).
outcome_detail: After a staff report, council voted to open the pool on Louis Riel Day and Victoria Day and close it on Remembrance Day.
mover: Councillor Penner (Susan or Cari; not distinguishable)
notes: The two Penners cannot be distinguished from these transcripts.

title: Other funding and support letters received as information
requester: KidSport; Better Business Bureau; Youth for Christ; Envision; Katie Cares; RCMP (Headway program); Crime Stoppers; Navy League of Canada; 'Cambridges' (as heard); Steinbach and Area Lions Club; Ronald McDonald House Charities; Agape House
ask: Grants, sponsorships or support: KidSport grant (Mar 21), Better Business Bureau sponsorship (Sep 5), Youth for Christ (Nov 7 and Nov 21), Envision, Katie Cares and RCMP Headway program funding (Nov 21), Crime Stoppers and Navy League (Dec 5), a 'Cambridges' grant, Lions Club program letter and Ronald McDonald House support (Dec 19); Agape House asked for a declaration (Dec 5).
tactics: Letters only; no delegations.
outcome_detail: No public decision: all were received as information with little or no discussion, some 'for now'. For the Agape House declaration the mayor only looked for a councillor to attend its Dec 6 event.
notes: Contents of these letters were not read aloud, so the amounts asked are unknown. Some 'for now' items may have been considered at budget time. Also filed as information without a clear ask: C.C. on community broadband (Mar 21), Partnership of the Manitoba Capital Region on transportation (Sep 19), a letter from the RM of Ste. Anne's CAO (Aug 15) and a letter from Mr. F. (Dec 19).

title: Sidewalk and traffic review on Albert Street
ask: Build a sidewalk on Albert Street and look at traffic there.
tactics: A request filed with council by A.M. and his spouse (traffic and children walking to school), repeated at the July 18 rezoning hearing; a councillor raised it again when the nearby care-home project was approved.
outcome_detail: Staff said there were no immediate plans; Councillor Siemens asked that it go to the next study session. No public decision was found in 2017.
notes: A.M.'s remarks were made during a planning public hearing (otherwise excluded), but the sidewalk/traffic request was a separate filed request; it did not appear in any searched agenda (it may have been on the unsearched April 4 meeting or handled administratively). Not confirmed whether it reached a study session.

title: Stop sign at Industrial Road and North Front Drive
ask: Add a stop sign at Industrial Road and North Front Drive so traffic from the diner's property can get out safely.
tactics: Letter asking for safer access from its property; staff had the city engineer review it before it reached council, and it mirrored a nearby stop-sign configuration; new motels being built behind the site.
outcome_detail: Approved the night it came to council, on the city manager's recommendation.
notes: Business name taken from the city manager's wording ('the diner on 52'); not confirmed against the letter.

title: Letter opposing federal small-business tax changes
ask: Support the Chamber's letter asking the federal government to drop its proposed small-business tax changes.
tactics: Chamber letter asking the city to back its letter to the federal Finance Minister; a councillor turned it into a motion with national statistics; timed during the national debate on the proposals.
outcome_detail: Council resolved to write to the federal government asking it to abandon the changes. On Nov 7 council received a form reply from the Finance Minister and noted the government had since made some changes.
mover: Councillor Penner (Susan or Cari; not distinguishable)
notes: The Chamber letter itself was not read aloud.

title: Longer no-parking zone on Reimer Avenue West
ask: Extend the no-parking zone on Reimer Avenue West near Harvest Drive.
tactics: Letter describing traffic and parking problems at Reimer Avenue West and Harvest Drive.
outcome_detail: Referred to administration by consensus; two weeks later, on the city engineer's review, council extended the no-parking zone to just west of the second leg of Cambridge Way.

title: Paving rule for businesses on gravel roads
requester: Councillor John Fehr, for business owners
ask: Revisit the zoning bylaw rule requiring hard-surfaced parking for businesses next to gravel roads.
tactics: Raised in question period after 'numerous' inquiries over six months to a year; another councillor reported the same.
outcome_detail: The mayor had staff flag it for the zoning bylaw review that the annexation was prompting; no bylaw change in 2017.
notes: On Dec 5, 2017 council heard a variance request from a business on a gravel road to waive paving (a planning hearing, so excluded here).

title: Hanover School Division: safer crossing at Barkman Avenue and Fourth Street
ask: Review the two-way stop at Barkman Ave & Fourth St and the speed zone on Barkman Ave (McKenzie to Fourth).
tactics: Second written request (first in May 2015, again Oct 13, 2017) asking the city to review the two-way stop at Barkman/Fourth and the speed zone on Barkman Avenue near the schools.
outcome_detail: Administration recommended keeping the two-way stop and the 50 km/h limit (adding only a no-stopping zone); council instead amended the traffic by-law to install a four-way stop, unanimously. The speed zone was not reduced.
notes: No transcript or video exists for Jan 16, 2018; everything comes from the minutes. Mayor Goertzen, Councillors C. Penner and Fehr were absent. Whether HSD specifically asked for a four-way stop is not stated in the minutes.

title: Parking and snow access at a community mailbox
ask: Change parking at the Third Street / Reimer Avenue community mailbox so he can get his mail in winter.
tactics: Letter from a new resident worried he could not reach his community mailbox at Third Street and Reimer Avenue in winter.
outcome_detail: Staff recommended no parking change and pointed to Canada Post's snow-clearing duty; council agreed to reply explaining the Canada Post agreement.
notes: The city manager said the letter was read 'at a council meeting on October 5th, 2017'; there was no Oct 5 meeting, so it was most likely the Oct 17 meeting, whose recording failed to transcribe. first_date is therefore approximate.

title: Hanover School Division: school-area traffic safety
ask: Review a reduced school-zone speed, a four-way stop and a pedestrian crossing near a school.
tactics: Follow-up letter after an earlier request (four-way stop at Barkman Avenue and Fourth Street) was answered only with parking changes; cited a student injury; three specific asks.
outcome_detail: Referred to administration by consensus for a report; no report back was found in 2017. The earlier four-way-stop request had been refused in favour of no-parking/no-stopping changes.
notes: Date of the earlier HSD four-way-stop request not found in 2017 transcripts (likely 2016). Check 2018 minutes for the staff report.

title: Paved shoulder on PTH 52 East
ask: A paved shoulder on PTH 52 East.
tactics: Email to council.
outcome_detail: Received as information without discussion; no public decision. PTH 52 is a provincial highway and no request to the province was made.
notes: Purpose of the shoulder (e.g., cycling or walking) not stated on the recording.

title: Steinbach Fly-In Golf Club: $500,000 grant, then land sale
ask: A $500,000 grant to stabilize the club's finances; after refusal, a city purchase of 40 acres for $500,000 with a $1/year leaseback.
tactics: Presented privately to council in closed meetings: first a $500,000 grant request citing financial difficulties (refused), then an offer to sell 40 acres of the course to the city for the same $500,000 with a $1-a-year leaseback for about 63 years; payment spread over 3 years. Supporters cited the club's private investment, contributions to paving and flood mitigation, about $2 million a year in local economic activity, and a Steinbach Chamber of Commerce letter endorsing the club.
outcome_detail: The grant was refused in closed session, but council approved buying the 40 acres for $500,000 (paid over 3 years, no appraisal mentioned) and leasing it back to the club for $1 a year until about 2083. The first public discussion was the night of the vote.
mover: Councillor John Fehr (purchase); lease mover not named, seconded by Councillor John Fehr
vote: purchase carried; tally not stated on the audio. Stated positions imply 4-3 (against: Michael Zwaagstra, Earl Funk, one Councillor Penner). Lease carried; Zwaagstra said he would vote against.
notes: Recording is audio only and diarization is unreliable (Councillor Zwaagstra's speech is split between labels I and G; G is otherwise the city manager). The original grant request was made 'just over a year ago' in a closed meeting (late 2016), so first_date is the first public mention. Classified 'won' because the club received the full $500,000 it first sought and kept using the land; it could be read as 'partly' since the grant itself was refused. Which Penner voted which way is not determinable here.

title: Narrow, treacherous Henry Street near the hospital
ask: Make Henry Street safer near the hospital (widen it or otherwise ease congestion).
tactics: Letter describing how tight and dangerous Henry Street is, especially in winter, with hospital traffic.
outcome_detail: Staff said the street is standard width and widening would need costly study; council took the letter as information 'for now', with no public decision.
notes: The writer's surname was garbled in the transcript, so the initials M.P. are uncertain. Henry Street parking near the hospital returned to council in 2023.

notes: Whether the zoning review later changed the limit is not known from 2017 records.

title: Accessible parking on Main Street
requester: Resident (Mr. C.; first name not given)
ask: Use the Main Street patio area for accessible (handicap) parking in winter.
tactics: Letter with a photo about drainage near a Main Street patio, suggesting the area be used for accessible parking in winter; a councillor who has used a wheelchair took it up.

vote: carried; Michael Zwaagstra said he would vote against; tally not stated

title: Ten grant/funding letters received as information
requester: Junior Achievement of Manitoba; Manitoba SwimAbility; Westman Opportunities Leadership and Support; KidSport Canada (Manitoba); enVision Foundation; Today House; Youth for Christ Steinbach; Steinbach Chamber of Commerce; Mennonite Heritage Village; Manitoba Crime Stoppers
ask: Grants or donations (amounts not stated in the minutes).

ask: Consider a 'volunteer park'.

notes: Minor; the letter's details are not in the minutes.

title: Pat Porter Active Living Centre: yearly grant in lieu of property taxes

title: STARS air ambulance: an annual municipal pledge
requester: STARS (M.K., G.T.); R.M. of Ste. Anne (letter)
ask: A pledge of annual support for STARS through the city's protective-services budget.
tactics: A neighbouring municipality's letter (Feb 20), then a STARS delegation (May 1) with mission counts (24 trips to Steinbach in a year), funding model (89% provincial), and the 'nearly 40 municipalities' already partnering; asked for money through the protective-services budget.
outcome_detail: The Ste. Anne letter was received as information; the delegation was thanked. No pledge or grant appears in the 2018 minutes.
notes: The 2022-26 report shows the city funding STARS each year; when that started (2019 or later) was not checked.

requester: Clearspring Greens / Rams Gate residents (S.J. as lead presenter, about 20 objectors at the hearing)
ask: Build the pathway without charging the neighbourhood most of the $625,000 cost (as was done for Deerfield).
tactics: Residents had asked for a safe pathway out of the neighbourhood since 2015 and met council in July 2019; when the city proposed a $625,000 local improvement charged to 146 parcels (about $4,281 each up front), they filed 16 written objections, filled the hearing (minutes list about 20 speakers; S.J. handed out a written brief with the original lot plans, the Deerfield precedent and possible gas-tax and provincial grant money), offered partial cost-sharing ideas, then kept objections alive for the Municipal Board (32 registered after the hearing, 78 by January 2021).
outcome_detail: On Jan 7 council gave the levy by-law first and second reading 5-2 after defeating a Siemens/J. Hiebert amendment to cut the scope (limestone, no lighting). On Jan 21 council moved the $208,000 lighting cost to the city reserve (6-1), cutting the estimate to about $2,800 per lot. Objections went to the Municipal Board; on 2021-01-05 council cancelled the 2020 plan (78 objections) and adopted a 50/50 split capped at $1,610 per parcel; the pathway was tendered in April 2021 (R21-011, R21-012, R21-077).
resolution_no: R20-003 (amendment defeated), R20-004/R20-005 (1st/2nd reading), R20-012 (city funds lighting)
mover: R20-004/005: Damian Penner; R20-012: Michael Zwaagstra
seconder: R20-004/005: Michael Zwaagstra; R20-012: Damian Penner
vote: R20-003 amendment defeated 2-5 (for: Siemens, J. Hiebert); R20-004/005 carried 5-2 (against: Siemens, J. Hiebert); R20-012 carried 6-1 (against: Siemens)
notes: The July 16, 2019 meeting the residents refer to falls in the 2019 period. Final 2021 terms (cancel By-law 2132; 50/50 split capped at $1,610 per parcel; new By-law 2168) are from steinbach_council_motions.csv (R21-011, R21-012, R21-031 to R21-033, R21-076, R21-077), not read in the 2021 transcripts.
